lesson.title: Making Plans Together
lesson.subtitle: Choices, hobbies and an afternoon with friends
lesson.description: Make plans with friends, choose between activities, explain why you need a break, and talk about your favourite sports.

learning_objectives: Offer two alternatives with 还是 (háishi) in a question.
Invite someone to do an activity together using 一起 (yìqǐ).
Give a reason using 所以 (suǒyǐ) and request a short break using 一会儿 (yíhuìr).
Express a favourite activity using 最 (zuì) and discuss sports naturally.

metadata.audience: HSK 3.0 Level 2 learners with HSK Level 1 foundation

overview.topic_description: Two friends choose how to spend an afternoon, make a plan to play football, and agree to take a break first.
overview.focus: Use 还是 (háishi) for either/or questions, 一起 (yìqǐ) for shared activities, 所以 (suǒyǐ) for reasons, and 最 (zuì) for favourites.

grammar_points.title: Choosing between alternatives
grammar_points.explanation: Use 还是 (háishi) between alternatives in a choice question. In this lesson, 还是 is not a connector for ordinary affirmative lists.

grammar_points.title: Making joint plans
grammar_points.explanation: Place 一起 (yìqǐ) before the action to say people do it together.

grammar_points.title: Giving a reason
grammar_points.explanation: Present a reason before 所以 (suǒyǐ), then explain its consequence.

grammar_points.title: Expressing what you like most
grammar_points.explanation: Use 最 (zuì) before a descriptive expression such as 喜欢 (xǐhuan) to express the highest degree.

dialogue.title: An afternoon plan
dialogue.context_en: Two classmates decide whether to play football or watch a movie, and agree on a short rest and a meeting time.

patterns.title: 还是 (háishi): ask which alternative
patterns.explanation_en: In a question, place 还是 (háishi) between two options. Answer by naming the option you prefer. Here it means “or” in a question; other meanings are learned separately.
patterns.formula_en: Option A + 还是 (háishi) + option B + ?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi hē shuǐ?
examples.english: Would you like tea or water?

examples.hanzi: 你明天想去学校还是在家学习？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān xiǎng qù xuéxiào háishi zài jiā xuéxí?
examples.english: Do you want to go to school or study at home tomorrow?

patterns.title: 一起 (yìqǐ): do something together
patterns.explanation_en: Place 一起 (yìqǐ) before the verb phrase. Use 和 (hé) to name the person accompanying you when needed.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé péngyou yìqǐ xué Zhōngwén.
examples.english: My friend and I study Chinese together.

examples.hanzi: 明天下午我们一起去运动。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān xiàwǔ wǒmen yìqǐ qù yùndòng.
examples.english: We will go exercise together tomorrow afternoon.

patterns.title: 所以 (suǒyǐ): explain the result
patterns.explanation_en: State a reason and then use 所以 (suǒyǐ) to introduce the result. You do not need an English-style “because” clause for this basic pattern.

examples.hanzi: 今天下雨，所以我们在家看电影。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒmen zài jiā kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: It is raining today, so we are watching a movie at home.

examples.hanzi: 他今天很忙，所以晚上不能来。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān hěn máng, suǒyǐ wǎnshang bù néng lái.
examples.english: He is busy today, so he cannot come tonight.

patterns.title: 最 (zuì): say what you like most
patterns.explanation_en: Place 最 (zuì) before 喜欢 (xǐhuan) to express the strongest preference within a set of possibilities.
patterns.formula_en: Person + 最 (zuì) + 喜欢 (xǐhuan) + activity or thing

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: I like watching movies most.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan shénme yùndòng?
examples.english: Which sport do you like most?

reading.title: Two friends make a Saturday plan

paragraphs.hanzi: 星期六下午，小美想和朋友一起运动。她最喜欢足球。小强今天有点儿累，所以想休息一会儿。
paragraphs.pinyin: Xīngqīliù xiàwǔ, Xiǎoměi xiǎng hé péngyou yìqǐ yùndòng. Tā zuì xǐhuan zúqiú. Xiǎoqiáng jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lèi, suǒyǐ xiǎng xiūxi yíhuìr.
paragraphs.english: On Saturday afternoon, Xiaomei wants to exercise with a friend. Football is her favourite. Xiaoqiang is a little tired today, so he wants to rest for a while.

paragraphs.hanzi: 小美问：“我们踢足球还是看电影？”小强说：“休息一会儿，我们再去踢足球吧！”他们下午三点在学校见。
paragraphs.pinyin: Xiǎoměi wèn: “Wǒmen tī zúqiú háishi kàn diànyǐng?” Xiǎoqiáng shuō: “Xiūxi yíhuìr, wǒmen zài qù tī zúqiú ba!” Tāmen xiàwǔ sān diǎn zài xuéxiào jiàn.
paragraphs.english: Xiaomei asks, “Shall we play football or watch a movie?” Xiaoqiang says, “Let’s rest a little, then go play football!” They meet at school at three in the afternoon.

teaching_plan.common_pitfall: In a two-option question, use 还是 (háishi) between the alternatives; do not treat it like “and.” Note that 还是 can also mean “still” in another context, which is not the use practised here. Put 一起 (yìqǐ) before the shared action, 最 (zuì) before 喜欢 (xǐhuan), and 所以 (suǒyǐ) before the consequence.
teaching_plan.pronunciation_focus: Compare 一起 (yìqǐ), where 一 (yī) is pronounced yì before a third tone, with 一会儿 (yíhuìr), where 一 becomes yí before a fourth tone. The source citation spelling for 一会儿 is yíhuìr, and 还是 (háishi) has a light second syllable. Keep 累 (lèi) as a fourth tone.

can_do: Offer friends two activities using 还是 (háishi).
Arrange a joint activity using 一起 (yìqǐ).
Explain that you feel tired and need a short rest using 所以 (suǒyǐ) and 一会儿 (yíhuìr).
State your favourite activity using 最喜欢 (zuì xǐhuan).
